:::{#thm-block-inverse}
#### The inverse of a positive definite block matrix

Let $\matr{X} = \begin{bmatrix} \matr{A} & \matr{B} \\ \tp{\matr{B}} & \matr{C} \end{bmatrix}$
be as in @thm-block-quadratic,
with $\matr{X}$ [positive definite](#def-positive-definite).
Then $\matr{X}$ is [invertible](#def-invertible-matrix),
and with the [Schur complement](#def-schur-complement) $\matr{S}$ of $\matr{A}$,
the last $m$ columns of its [inverse](#def-matrix-inverse) are

$$
\matr{X}^{-1}
= \begin{bmatrix}
\matr{P} & -\matr{A}^{-1} \matr{B} \matr{S}^{-1} \\
-\matr{S}^{-1} \tp{\matr{B}} \matr{A}^{-1} & \matr{S}^{-1}
\end{bmatrix},
$$

where $\matr{P}$ holds the first $k$ rows and columns of $\matr{X}^{-1}$.

:::

::: proof

[$\matr{X}$ is invertible](#thm-pd-inverse), because it is [positive definite](#def-positive-definite).
By the [Schur complement test](#thm-schur-test), $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{S}$ are positive definite as well,
and [so both are invertible](#thm-pd-inverse).
Let $\matr{W} = \begin{bmatrix} -\matr{A}^{-1}\matr{B} \\ \matr{I}_m \end{bmatrix}$.
Each entry of $\matr{X}\matr{W}$ adds one group of $k$ summands to one group of $m$ summands,
so $\matr{X}\matr{W}$ can be computed one block row at a time:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\matr{X}\matr{W}
&= \begin{bmatrix}
-\matr{A}\matr{A}^{-1}\matr{B} + \matr{B} \\
-\tp{\matr{B}}\matr{A}^{-1}\matr{B} + \matr{C}
\end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(one block row at a time)} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix} -\matr{I}_k\matr{B} + \matr{B} \\ \matr{S} \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(} \matr{A}\matr{A}^{-1} = \matr{I}_k \text{, and definition of } \matr{S} \text{)} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix} \matr{0} \\ \matr{S} \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(} \matr{I}_k\matr{B} = \matr{B} \text{)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides on the left by $\matr{X}^{-1}$ gives $\matr{W}$ on the left,
since $\matr{X}^{-1}\matr{X} = \matr{I}_{k+m}$.
Cut $\matr{X}^{-1}$ into the four pieces $\matr{P}$, $\matr{Q}$, $\matr{R}$ and $\matr{T}$,
with $\matr{Q}$ and $\matr{T}$ in the last $m$ columns.
Then the right side is $\matr{X}^{-1}\begin{bmatrix} \matr{0} \\ \matr{S} \end{bmatrix}$,
and the last $m$ columns of $\matr{X}^{-1}$ multiply $\matr{S}$:

$$
\begin{bmatrix} -\matr{A}^{-1}\matr{B} \\ \matr{I}_m \end{bmatrix}
= \begin{bmatrix} \matr{Q}\matr{S} \\ \matr{T}\matr{S} \end{bmatrix}.
$$

So $\matr{T}\matr{S} = \matr{I}_m$ and $\matr{Q}\matr{S} = -\matr{A}^{-1}\matr{B}$.
Multiplying both equations on the right by $\matr{S}^{-1}$ gives
$\matr{T} = \matr{S}^{-1}$ and $\matr{Q} = -\matr{A}^{-1}\matr{B}\matr{S}^{-1}$.
$\matr{X}^{-1}$ is [symmetric](#def-symmetric-matrix),
by [the inverse of a symmetric matrix is symmetric](#cor-inverse-symmetric),
so $\matr{R} = \tp{\matr{Q}} = -\matr{S}^{-1}\tp{\matr{B}}\matr{A}^{-1}$,
using $\tp{(\matr{S}^{-1})} = \matr{S}^{-1}$ and $\tp{(\matr{A}^{-1})} = \matr{A}^{-1}$.

:::
